This routine is for anyone who is not dealing with extreme damage but wants over all glossier & softer hair this is the the exact routine I built for getting glass hair on fine hair but will work for the wavy curly hair girls too!!  the science: the flatten your cuticle lies, the more light it reflects that's what gives the illusion of glass. glossy hair isn't a product, it's the consistency of routine over time that’s keeping that cuticle smooth from prewash to final styling  it took me a while to figure out the system, but once I did, the results compounded and now I wanna share my favourite tips with you because this is the routine that actually for every  wash day. the 5 things I never skip: 1. always create a barrier before shampoo: hair oil or conditioner first. less friction = less cuticle damage = more shine 2. weekly hair mask. deep hydration is what keeps that cuticle flat and the shine consistent. 3. a glossing treatment every 3-4 weeks  this is the step that takes glossy to glass  4. leave-in conditioner every single wash. beats frizz and keeps the cuticle flat between washes. 5. the hair sandwich method oil before heat styling AND after. then always finish with a cool shot to lock the cuticle in place ✨ Hope these haircare tips help you guys!! #hair #haircare #glasshair #hairgloss

Please check it out when you can!🫶🏽💕 Our nighttime routine is now filled with pet care for Baby, which happens to look just like Bown’s 🥺 A big part of Baby’s pet night routine is making sure she’s comfortable and cared for before bed. Every evening, we do one of her twice-daily bandage changes, check her arm, clean the area, and make sure everything looks good before settling in for the night. Plus she also gets her medications and supplements. It’s not exactly the cozy pet night routine I imagined years ago, but it’s become part of how we care for her and help keep her comfortable, and it’s our version of cozy! She also looks forward to all the treats she gets!🐾🦴 At 15 and a half years old, Baby is managing cancer, Addison’s disease, mitral valve disease, pulmonary hypertension, a heart murmur, and vestibular disease. Despite everything on that list, she’s still doing remarkably well and continues to enjoy her daily routines, meals, cuddles, and bedtime rituals.🥹 In many ways, we’re in a very similar situation to what we experienced with Bown. The biggest difference is that we’re currently able to keep Baby on her chemotherapy medication while continuing to manage her arm. We’re grateful for every day that she’s responding well and able to maintain her quality of life and so far she loves being here and being center of my entire universe! I love being her mommy!  A good night routine helps pets feel safe, comfortable, and cared for. For us, that means medications, bandage changes, monitoring her progress, plenty of affection, and making sure she’s ready to get a good night’s rest. One thing I’ve learned through caring for senior dogs with complex medical conditions is that consistency matters. The little things — staying on schedule with treatments, paying attention to changes, and creating a calm bedtime routine — can make a big difference. My dogs love their nighttime music so I have to make sure I play that or they will not settle in!  Tonight’s routine may look a little different than most, but seeing Baby settle in comfortably at the end of the day is always worth it!❤️ I would like to thank all of you who have been with us through the journey with Bown through losing him, and now being here for Baby. it’s been very hard to get back to posting on this page as you could imagine there’s a pretty big void missing for me, but I’m really trying my best to honor the life and legacy that my sweet boy left behind and continuing to manage my sweet girl.
